label: Premise
description: The seed of the book: who the story is chiefly about, what stands against them, what they stand to lose and the question that keeps a reader going. A book usually has one.

fields.label: Central character
fields.help: Who the story is chiefly about, in a short phrase; the full profile belongs in that character's own entry.

fields.label: Starting situation
fields.help: How things stand for the central character when the story opens, before the trouble begins.

fields.label: Central conflict
fields.help: What stands against the central character, and why they cannot simply walk away from it.

fields.label: Stakes
fields.help: What the central character, or the people around them, would lose if they fail.

fields.label: Why this character
fields.help: Why this particular person must face this conflict, whether because they are best equipped for it or least suited to it.

fields.label: Scope of the conflict
fields.help: How far beyond the central character the outcome of the conflict reaches.

fields.label: Inner and outer conflict
fields.help: How much of the central conflict is fought within the central character rather than against the world around them.

fields.label: Story question
fields.help: The one question a reader keeps reading to see settled, written as a question the ending must close.

fields.label: Distinctive angle
fields.help: What sets this premise apart from familiar stories of its kind, as you see it.

fields.label: Genre expectations
fields.help: Conventions readers of this genre will expect the premise to honour, and any it means to turn on their head.

fields.label: Direction of the outcome
fields.help: Which way you currently expect the story question to be settled for the central character.

fields.label: Known weak points
fields.help: Doubts you already hold about the premise, such as plausibility, familiarity or thin stakes, to test in later sessions.

fields.label: Part played
fields.help: What the one does in or for the other: who acts, who is acted upon, who only looks on.

fields.label: What it leaves behind
fields.help: What this involvement costs, wins or changes for either side once it is over.

fields.label: What holds it together
fields.help: Why this link exists: the need, duty, fear, belief or bargain that keeps it in place.

fields.label: What each side gives and gets
fields.help: What passes between the two because of this link, such as loyalty, protection, money, secrets or obedience.

fields.label: Where it strains
fields.help: The pressure that could break or turn this link, and what would follow if it gave way.

fields.label: How it changes
fields.help: Where this link stands at the start of the book and at its end, and what moves it.

fields.label: How they fit together
fields.help: What each contributes to the other, and how the part sits within the whole.

fields.label: What sets them apart
fields.help: What one holds that the other lacks, so that the two never blur together.

fields.label: How it shows on the page
fields.help: Where and how the reader meets this link: in an action, an image, a setting or a choice.

fields.label: Why it matters
fields.help: What this link does for the book: the meaning, pressure or effect it carries.

fields.label: Where they meet or part
fields.help: The point on which the two stand against each other: one question answered two ways.

fields.label: What the comparison reveals
fields.help: What a reader understands from setting the two side by side that neither shows alone.
